sources.title: ThinkRail — product goal and scope
sources.locator: Value; Principles; Capabilities; Non-goals
sources.finding: pi is the only engine, run in-process, with no second runtime. Git, GitHub and model access go through the user-owned git, gh and central CLI plus pi provider auth; ThinkRail keeps no accounts or tokens. Cloned-repository resources and repo MCP servers load only after a per-project trust grant. Capabilities include projects-to-workspaces, scratch chats, concurrent steerable chats, plans with per-step independent review, subagents and background commands, agent-started workspaces, anchored review comments, PR open/update via gh, specs, workflows, providers, pi config, agent tools, pi packages and MCP. Desktop profile is local only; a later shared-client profile can dial an existing host. Bundled extensions pi-spec-graph, pi-thinkrail-workflow and pi-todos; portable packages pi-delegation, pi-background-commands and pi-subagents (Agent plus get_subagent_result tools) bundled into every parent session.

sources.finding: Background commands are session-owned with start, list, output and stop; at most 8 active with the latest 20 finished records retained.

sources.title: ThinkRail v0.3.2 — sessionHost.ts
sources.locator: MCP_CONFIRM_ALWAYS; confirm() on data-changing calls with no-UI-attached fallback; allow once/chat/always
sources.finding: MCP confirmation is product code: data-changing calls confirm with Deny, Allow once, Allow in this chat or Always allow, and fail closed with no UI attached.

sources.finding: Fixed external-editor launcher list (VS Code, Emacs, JetBrains IDEs, Vim). No ThinkRail editor extension ships.

sources.title: ThinkRail v0.3.2 — index.ts

sources.finding: Spec CRUD plus validate and grep tools; the index revalidates by mtime/size and never serves stale. No approval, citation or conflict-detection tools.

sources.title: ThinkRail native Pi subscription authentication
sources.locator: anthropicExtraUsage.ts anthropicSubscriptionAuthActive; auth/providerLogin.ts startLogin; auth/detectAccounts.ts known subscription plans
sources.finding: ThinkRail starts Pi's own OAuth login flow, and its runtime explicitly recognizes active Anthropic subscription OAuth credentials for extra-usage warnings. Detected Claude/Codex CLI account plans are setup signals, not borrowed credentials. This establishes subscription use through the embedded Pi provider login rather than a separate CLI runtime.
